title: Terbinafine high dose versus standard dose for tinea capitis in children (TINEA TINEA)
official: Terbinafine high dose versus standard dose for tinea capitis in children (TINEA TINEA)
summary: Main objective: To compare the efficacy of a high dose of oral terbinafine versus a standard dose in achieving a clinical cure (defined as a regression of symptoms, i.e., clear or almost clear) with a negative mycological culture at W4.
conditions: Dermatophytosis of the scalp hair (Tinea capitis)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient aged >2 years and <18 years
2. Weight ≥ 10 kg
3. Diagnosis of Tinea Capitis based on clinical examination
4. Ability to comply with the requirements of the study
5. Patient covered by or entitled to social security
6. Written informed consent obtained from the patient’s legal representatives
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient previously included in the study for a previous episod of Tinea Capitis
2. Patients with mycological culture results available at the inclusion
3. Siblings consulting on the same day for TC (risk of treatment administration errors if siblings are allocated to different study arms)
4. Patient with uncertain or doubtful diagnoses of Tinea Capitis
5. Contra indication to terbinafine: renal failure (eGFR<30), known chronic or active liver disease, hypersensitivity
6. Contra indication to topicat antifungal treatment: hypersensitivity
7. Pregnant/breastfeeding woman
8. Young-woman of child-bearing potential who are not using an acceptable birth control method
9. Previous treatment with systemic antifungals (within 3 months)
10. Previous treatment with topical antifungal (within 2 weeks)
11. Ongoing treatement with deutetrabenazine or tetrabenazine
sponsor: Centre Hospitalier Regional Universitaire De Tours
